feature: A component sheet that starts on its title's edge, with parts kept inside their boxes
summary: A component sheet now starts on its title's left edge and ends the same distance from the right. Ask keeps a card's buttons and words inside the card, wraps long words in a tall box, and shows Off, Default and On looks that mean what they say: no tick in an unchecked box, a grey Off switch, the knob at the far end when On, a visible tick when checked.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a blank 1440 x 1024 picture and press Ask.

try.do: Press Ask and type: create a table of apple like quality base components that show different states and text
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Check the title and the row names: they start on one left edge, and the last column ends the same distance from the right.
Look at the Off checkbox and the Off switch: the box is empty and the switch is grey.
Ask for: Make a component sheet for a website's design system: buttons, text fields, cards and navigation, each labelled, with a title.
Read a card's description: it wraps onto two lines inside the card.
Ask the Photonz skill in an agent session for the same two sheets and compare.
Look at the skill's design sheet: every section has its header row, the cards included.
Press Command Z once: the whole sheet goes.

evaluate: Does the sheet read as one page now that the table starts on the title's edge?
Is a 64 point margin on both sides the right room for a sheet, or should it be wider?
Do the Off, Default and On looks read as their state at a glance?
With most rows having two states under a four-column grid, does the empty right side bother you?
rough: Not at the bar yet, so the task stays open. Skill (rubric f5ae1562): your request 87.6 (judge 8, 8, 7, 8, 9), the design sheet 87.2 (8, 8, 7, 8, 9); before this pass 86 and 81.2 to 85.6. Aligned is still 7: controls of different widths share a column, a slider sits among the button rows, and navigation bars reach near the right margin.

Ask on this Mac: your request 51.7 (judge 6, 6, 6, 5, 5), the design sheet 78.8 (7, 7, 6, 6, 7); earlier runs on this pass gave 42.6 to 56.6 and 18.3 to 76. The 18.3 was a card refused twelve times because a wrapping body was read as one line, fixed here. One component-table run never got a first answer from the model in five minutes and was run again; that stall is find-out-why-ask-sometimes-waits-five-minutes-fo.

What holds Ask back is still its own looks: hover looks that barely differ from default, a Disabled field darker than its Default, a look named Selected2, a tick drawn blue on the blue box (fixed after the last eval, not yet measured).
Four columns stretch across the page while most of Ask's rows have two states, so the right half reads empty to judges.
The name chips the canvas puts over each component copy cover the header row in the window picture. Already its own task: the-name-chips-over-component-copies-stay-clear.
No mock covers the component sheet; it is judged against Apple's design kit pages.
